svg.title: Who Touches a Form 211 Claim
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-irs-whistleblower-office-architecture; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Who Touches a Form 211 Claim; subtitle: The Whistleblower Office bottleneck and the lanes around it; caption: About 1,000 claims a month reach 32 reviewers, so only documented, insider-sourced, collectible claims above the $2,000,000 floor get traction, and nothing pays until appeals are exhausted.; assumptions note: Intake load, reviewer count, and thresholds are practitioner-reported; Brown adds that the IRS rarely moves below a likely $10 million collection.; note: Sources: Where IRS Problems Get Solved (Eric Green, ruRW_hNSDYk), The Anti-Fraud Coalition (Emily Stibil, fQss6bE5tKc), Brown, LLC (tQIkb01vCTw), Former IRS Agent Representation (41ejxu80Qtg, QxVllUQ7IRk), Logan Allec (i4GnKgGXiMw).; center: role: IRS Whistleblower Office; headcount: 32 reviewers; focus: About 1,000 claims per month, roughly 30 to 35 new files per reviewer each month; spokes: role: Named whistleblower filing Form 211; type: Claimant; kpi: More than $2,000,000 in dispute; over $200,000 gross income for individual targets; role: Whistleblower counsel; type: Claim packaging; kpi: Narrative memo with enabling-party, witness, and document appendices handed over on day one; role: Examination and collection; type: Collection gate; kpi: Collection potential proven before filing; 15 to 30 percent paid only on proceeds collected; role: IRS Criminal Investigation; type: Prosecution lane; kpi: Conviction rates rather than collections; wants a large, near-perfect case
